text:
Michael McCarron is 6-foot-6, came over from Nashville, and does the heavy work for Minnesota: 60 hits and 21 blocks in 20 games on about 14 minutes a night. What's new is the scoring. He has four goals and nine points, including the 4-2 goal in Toronto on Thursday, and the Wild have won eight of the last ten games he has played.

The hot stretch is earned. He has 2.4 expected goals on his own shots over his last ten against 1.6 usual, and the Wild have taken 59.3% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with him out there, 7.5 points better than when he sits. That last number is the one to trust least: his on-ice shooting is running hot.

His real value is still defensive. Evolving-Hockey had opponents getting fewer expected goals with him on the ice last season (90th percentile), even while rating him near replacement overall. He missed a game with an upper-body injury in early November and came straight back. What to watch: whether the goals keep coming once the bounces even out.
headline: McCarron is scoring in a role built for stopping goals
